name: Perplexity
summary: AI answer engine with cited sources.

flows.title: Ask a question and keep the follow-ups together
steps: Go to the search query box on the homepage and type your question. A session keeps your first question, every follow-up, Perplexity's answers and the sources behind them together.
A paid subscriber can pick a Search Mode — Pro, Research, or Create files and apps — and an AI model.
Sources can be narrowed, to Web or Academic, and files attached to the question.
The microphone icon dictates the question instead of typing it.
Ask follow-ups in the same session; it keeps the context, so earlier background does not have to be repeated.

flows.title: Find, tidy or share an earlier session
steps: Go to your History at perplexity.ai/library, which only you can see.
Use the search bar to find a session, Type to sort by Search Mode, and Sorting to go newest-to-oldest or the other way; sessions from the Comet browser can be hidden or shown.

Click Select to pick several sessions at once for deletion, or the three dots on one session to delete it or add it to a project. The dots menu on the right of the screen removes every session in one go.
To share a session, open it and click Share at the top right, then choose Private, Anyone with the link, or — for Enterprise Pro — anyone in your organization with the link.
Export saves the answer as PDF, Markdown or DOCX; Rewrite answers again with a different model.

flows.title: Make a skill for Perplexity Computer
steps: In Computer, go to the Skills page. Its two tabs are My Skills, which holds what you made or uploaded, and Perplexity Skills, the built-in library.
Select Create with Perplexity, then describe the task the skill should handle — Perplexity builds it with you through a conversation, and no technical knowledge is needed.

To bring in a skill you already have, select Upload a skill instead and drag in a .zip with a SKILL.md at the root, or a .md file, up to 10 MB. The file needs YAML frontmatter with a name and a description, and the name is lowercase with hyphens.
Write the description carefully: Perplexity reads it to decide when the skill applies, so it should carry the words somebody would use when they want it.
